key_insight: For a natural class of nonconvex functions, SGD with learning rate decay provably needs exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than any fixed learning rate in the small-step-size regime.
engineering_relevance: The result gives theoretical support for learning rate decay when seeking global optima on qualifying nonconvex objectives.
method: Analyze a nonconvex function class that includes many popular benchmark functions.
Compare gradient-query complexity for decaying versus fixed learning rates.
Use weak Poincaré inequalities to prove polynomial-time annealing for the associated non-logconcave sampling task.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity guarantees, but no numerical experiments or empirical performance measurements.
watch_item: The exponential advantage is established for a specific function class and small-step-size fixed-rate comparisons, not arbitrary nonconvex problems or practical training schedules.
paper_title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
